title: Four generations of musicians and starting dance bands at 13
summary: Music has come down three generations, with a grandson drumming at nine and hoped-for fourth; she started in dance bands at 13.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Getting my first drums, with or without lessons

blocks.x: No, no, no, never did. It has come down the line. I am now with the third generation.
Then I have a grandson that's playing drums, and I hope to be with him. He's nine years old.
But I hope to live long enough to make that fourth generation.
It would be nice, wouldn't it? Yeah. Only if he lives in, I mean, if you all keep playing, another five or six years, you'll be ready.
I'm sure you will. They don't start as young, though, now as they used to, Harley. Do they?
Well, this kid started since he was two years old.

Oh, really? I mean, going out to play music like they did in the old days. Well, there's some laws against it now. I guess there is. Like you said, you were playing in dance bands when you were 16 or so. Oh, 13 I started in dance bands. 13, yeah. 13. 13. Yeah. Mm-hmm. Mm-hmm. So Harley would see a girl doing that now. Okay.

Well, I was just a great big girl, you know. And if you just look at me, you would never say I was 13. Yeah. So I could pass that way, you see. A lot of children. I could never question my age. Yeah. But nevertheless, I was 13 years old.
